# Affected objects

Builds a consolidated inventory of all objects ("affected objects") involved in a Maester test run —
Microsoft Entra ID objects, tenant-level configuration surfaces, Microsoft Graph resources,
and external systems such as GitHub. The result is attached to the Maester results object as
the top-level `AffectedObjects` property, written to `<name>-affected-objects.json` (and
`<name>-affected-objects.csv` with `-ExportCsv`), and rendered on the **Affected objects** page of the HTML report.

## Opting in

Collection is off by default: `Invoke-Maester -IncludeAffectedObjects` turns it on and the html
report then offers the **Affected objects** page. The switch sets
`$__MtSession.IncludeAffectedObjects`, which gates the per-test `RelatedObjects` capture in
`Add-MtTestResultDetail`, and is passed to `ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult`, which gates the merge
and the `AffectedObjects` property. A report generated without it carries none of this data (no
`RelatedObjects` on the test results, no affected objects entries in `OutputFiles`) and the report's
sidebar does not offer the page.

`-RedactUserIdentity` needs the inventory to know which values belong to which user, so it
collects one even when `-IncludeAffectedObjects` was not passed. In that case `Invoke-Maester`
removes the `AffectedObjects` property again once the replacement map has been built, so the
report does not grow and the page does not appear unasked.

`Get-MtHtmlReport` embeds a slim copy: per record only `System`, `Type`, `Id`, `DisplayName`,
`PortalLink`, `Tests` and a `Referenced` flag (true when a check pointed at the object rather than
only the request cache), and no `RelatedObjects` on the tests. The JSON output and the objects
files keep the full records.

The page also needs a report template built from current `/report/src`. If
`<name>-affected-objects.json` was written but the sidebar has no Affected objects entry, the check-in
artifact `powershell/assets/ReportTemplate.html` is stale — see the stale template
troubleshooting section in [report/README.md](../../../report/README.md).

## Record schema

Every source normalizes into the same record shape so results can be merged and deduplicated:

| Field               | Description                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `System`            | Where the object lives: `EntraID`, `MicrosoftGraph`, `DefenderXDR`, `ExchangeOnline`, `GitHub`, ...               |
| `AnchorKind`        | How the object is identified — see [Anchor kinds](#anchor-kinds)                                                  |
| `Type`              | Canonical object type (`ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `User`, `Group`, `ServicePrincipal`, Graph resource path, ...) |
| `Id`                | Object id (GUID), resource key (`Fido2`), or external identity (`org/repo`); `$null` for singletons/collections  |
| `DisplayName`       | Human-readable name when the source provides one                                                                 |
| `UserPrincipalName` | UPN of a user object when the source provides one; used by PII redaction                                          |
| `PortalLink`        | Admin-portal deep link when a template exists for the type                                                       |
| `Tests`             | Test ids (`MT.xxxx`, ...) that referenced the object (aggregated)                                                 |
| `Sources`           | Which of the three detection sources found it (aggregated)                                                       |

## Anchor kinds

The classification answers "what kind of identifier anchors this object?":

- **Instance** — a single addressable object with its own id (a CA policy, a user, a group,
  a service principal, a transport rule). Strongest anchor; usually has a portal deep link.
- **Singleton** — a tenant-level configuration resource with no id; the Graph URI itself is
  the identity (`policies/authorizationPolicy`, `settings`). All EIDSCA checks anchor here.
- **Surface** — a portal settings page that a check points to without addressing a specific
  object (e.g. the Authentication Methods blade).
- **Collection** — a Graph collection read (`users`, `servicePrincipals`); records that the
  run touched the data set, not a specific member.
- **External** — an object outside Microsoft Graph, identified by its API path
  (GitHub organization/repository, Azure DevOps organization).
- **Unknown** — a structured object without an id (an instance type passed with no `id`, or
  an object with neither type nor id). It is not addressable, so it gets no portal link.

## The three detection sources

Detection runs in `ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult` (wrapped in try/catch — inventory problems
never fail a test run) via `Get-MtAffectedObject`, w

| Everything else | Systems absent from `KnownTypes` (`MicrosoftGraph`) pass through unchanged — their `Type` is a Graph resource path and cannot be enumerated. |

Currently inventoried: `EntraID` — AccessPackage, AccessPackageCatalog, AppRegistration,
AuthenticationMethod, AuthorizationPolicy, ConditionalAccessPolicy, ConsentPolicy, Device,
DirectoryRole, Domains, Group, ServicePrincipal, User; `DefenderXDR` — Device;
`ExchangeOnline` — SharingPolicy, TransportRule; `GitHub` — GitHubOrganization,
GitHubRepository, GitHubResource.

Excluded: `EntraID` — `EntraRecommendation`, `PimAlert`. Both describe a condition of the
tenant (a recommendation, an alert), not an addressable object, so they are findings that
belong in the test result, not rows in an object inventory.

A record of a curated system whose type is **not** in either list is dropped and reported in
a single `Write-Warning` summary (`System/Type (count)`), so a newly linked object type shows
up as an explicit maintenance item instead of silently reaching the report. Add it to
`KnownTypes` to inventory it, or to `ExcludedTypes` if it is not an affected object.

`ConvertTo-MtAffectedObjectRecord` also resolves type aliases before the record is built:
`IdentityProtection` objects are the users at risk, so they are recorded as `User`
(`Instance` with a user profile deep link) rather than as the Identity Protection blade.

## Extending detection

- **New portal deep-link pattern** → add a row to the regex table in
  `Get-MtAffectedObjectFromMarkdown` (keep more specific patterns first; the first capture
  group must be the id).
- **New `-GraphObjectType`** → add the ValidateSet entry in `Add-MtTestResultDetail`,
  the link template + instance flag in `Get-MtPortalLinkTemplate`,
  and (if the markdown parser has a matching pattern) the canonical name mapping in
  `ConvertTo-MtAffectedObjectRecord`.
- **New external system** → extend the cache walker in `Get-MtAffectedObjectFromCache`
  (or add a new source function and merge it in `Get-MtAffectedObject`).
- **New object type reaching the inventory** → add it to `Get-MtAffectedObjectTypeDefinition`
  (`KnownTypes` to keep it, `ExcludedTypes` to drop it); until then it is filtered out and
  named in the dropped-types warning.

## Redacting user identities

`Get-MtUserIdentityReplacementMap` turns the inventory's `User` objects into a map of
display name / UPN / object id → `UniqueId`. `Invoke-Maester` also passes `-IncludeSessionCache`,
which adds the UPN and object id (not the display name) of every user object in the cached Graph
responses, including users only read as part of a list, such as the member users MT.1033 names in
its test titles. The signed-in account (`Account`, `MgContext.Account`) is always mapped, since
every report carries it. `ConvertTo-MtRedactedReportContent` applies that map to rendered
report content, matching case-insensitively (UPNs and object ids are case-insensitive) and on word boundaries so a short display name cannot rewrite the middle
of an unrelated word (a service account named `Test` must not turn `TestResult` into a token).
With `-JsonEncoded` only json string values are rewritten, never property names, so a user
named like a property (`Severity`) cannot leave the report unparseable. Object ids and UPNs are
found by their shape and looked up in a dictionary, and only the remaining values (display names
and escaped forms) go into a regex alternation, so a tenant with tens of thousands of cached users
does not slow redaction down. `Get-MtAffectedObjectUniqueId` is the
single place the id is derived, so the html report, the json/markdown exports and the objects
files all use the same token. It lower-cases the `System|Type|Id` identity before hashing,
because the grouping that feeds it is case-insensitive while URL casing is not stable across
runs.

Redaction is pseudonymization, not anonymization: `UniqueId` is an unsalted SHA-256 over the
object identity with no tenant component, so a token is reversible by anyone holding a list of
candidate ids or UPNs, and the same user yields the same token in every tenant's report.

Redaction against json must pass `-JsonEncoded`: `ConvertTo-Json` escapes quotes, backslashes
and (on Windows PowerShell) non-ASCII characters, so the raw display name alone would not match
the serialized text. Display names shorter than four characters are skipped because a
substring replacement of them would corrupt unrelated words.

`Invoke-Maester -RedactUserIdentity` selects the scope: `None`, `HtmlOnly` (html report only) or
`AllOutputs` (every output).

## Offline validation

Offline validation without a tenant: mock `$__MtSession` (AdminPortalUrl + caches), stub
`Write-MtProgress`/`Get-MtPesterTagValue`/`Get-MtTestResultTemplate`/`Get-MtSkippedReason`,
dot-source the functions above, and assert on the produced records.

## The three detection sources

Detection runs in `ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult` (wrapped in try/catch — inventory problems
never fail a test run) via `Get-MtAffectedObject`, which merges three independent sources:

### 1. Structured capture — `RelatedObjects` (strongest, per-test attribution)

When a test calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -GraphObjects ...`, the objects are converted by
`ConvertTo-MtAffectedObjectRecord` into records **before** they are flattened into result markdown
(previously the ids were lost at that point). Type resolution, in order:

1. Explicit `-GraphObjectType` parameter, mapped to a canonical type name
   (`ConditionalAccess` → `ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `Users`/`UserRole` → `User`,
   `Groups` → `Group`, `Devices` → `Device`) so records dedupe against source 2.
2. `@odata.type` sniffing per object (`#microsoft.graph.user` → `User`, etc.), using the
   shared mapping in `Get-MtPortalLinkTemplate`, plus object-only mappings for
   `servicePrincipal`, `directoryRole` and `conditionalAccessPolicy`.
3. Other types are still captured: the raw `@odata.type` becomes the `Type`, and the record
   is an `Instance` if the object has an id. Unless the type is added to the catalog, the
   type filter then drops it with a warning (see below).

Portal deep links come from the same shared template table (`Get-MtPortalLinkTemplate`),
which is environment-aware via `$__MtSession.AdminPortalUrl` (Global/USGov/China clouds).
The records are stored per test in `$__MtSession.TestResultDetail[<test>].RelatedObjects`
and flow into the report JSON under `Tests[n].ResultDetail.RelatedObjects`.

### 2. Markdown deep-link parsing (covers ad-hoc links and old reports)

`Get-MtAffectedObjectFromMarkdown` enumerates the links in each test's rendered result
markdown (`ResultDetail.TestResult`) once, then tests every URL it finds against a regex table
of the known admin-portal deep-link patterns used across the shipped checks — the URL blade
pattern acts as a type system:

| URL pattern (fragment)                                        | Type                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/PolicyBlade/policyId/{guid}` | ConditionalAccessPolicy        |
| `ManagedAppMenuBlade/~/*/objectId/{guid}[/appId/{guid}]`      | ServicePrincipal               |
| `ApplicationMenuBlade/~/*/appId/{guid}`                       | AppRegistration                |
| `UserProfileMenuBlade/~/*/userId/{guid}`                      | User                           |
| `GroupDetailsMenuBlade/~/*/groupId/{guid}`                    | Group                          |
| `DeviceDetailsMenuBlade/~/*/objectId/{guid}`                  | Device                         |
| `Microsoft_Azure_ELMAdmin/CatalogBlade/catalogId/{guid}`      | AccessPackageCatalog           |
| `EntitlementMenuBlade/~/overview/entitlementId/{guid}`        | AccessPackage                  |
| `Microsoft_Azure_PIMCommon/AlertDetail/.../alertId/{id}`      | PimAlert                       |
| `RecommendationDetails.ReactView/recommendationId/{id}`       | EntraRecommendation            |
| `security.microsoft.com/machines/v2/{deviceId}`               | Device (DefenderXDR)           |
| `admin.exchange.microsoft.com .../ruleDetails/{guid}`         | TransportRule (ExchangeOnline) |
| `.../individualsharingdetails/{id}`                           | SharingPolicy (ExchangeOnline) |

The first pattern that matches a URL owns it, so ordering resolves overlaps (a service
principal URL also satisfies the less specific app registration pattern). The matched URL
becomes the record's `PortalLink`, and when it sits inside a markdown link `[name](url)` the
display name is recovered from the link that owns it. The name may contain one level of
brackets (`[[RaviK] - Policy](url)`), the URL may carry a link title (`[name](url "title")`),
and markdown escapes such as `\(` and `\_` are removed from the name. Links with an empty target
whose text is a UPN (`[user@contoso.com]()`, as the Entra recommendation checks list affected
users) become `User` records keyed by that UPN; `Get-MtAffectedObject` re-keys them to the
user's object id when the run saw it, so each user is one object. Only `https://` URLs are considered:
display names are not escaped in result markdown, so a crafted name could otherwise smuggle a
`javascript:` URL into the Affected objects page.
This source catches the ~55 checks that build `$portalLink` strings by hand (XSPM, CISA
Exchange, PIM, entitlement management, ...) without going through `Get-GraphObjectMarkdown`,
and it works post-hoc on any previously collected report JSON.

# Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment pack

The [Zero Trust Assessment](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) is Microsoft's free tool that checks a tenant
against Microsoft's Zero Trust guidance, across identity, devices, network, data, AI and security operations, and
says how to fix what it finds.
[Try the demo report](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment/demo) to see what it covers.

This pack runs the assessment from Maester and shows each of its results in the Maester report, next to Maester's
own checks. It ships with Maester and runs only when you ask for it.

Each result is one row, `ZTA.<assessment test ID>` (for example `ZTA.21770`), with the assessment's title, risk
level (as the severity), description, remediation steps and findings. Results are tagged `ZeroTrust` and
`ZeroTrust.<pillar>` (`ZeroTrust.Identity`, `ZeroTrust.Devices` and so on).

## Report an issue with a test

Microsoft writes and maintains the assessment's tests. If a test's result, text or remediation looks wrong, raise
it in [microsoft/zerotrustassessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment/issues). Problems with
running the pack from Maester go to [maester365/maester](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues).

## Run it

Install the assessment's module once, connect Maester to the tenant, then name the pack:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -SkipBuiltIn    # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA                 # Maester's tests and the assessment
```

The assessment runs in its own PowerShell process, so Maester signs in there for you. After an interactive
`Connect-Maester` you sign in a second time, in the browser. Without a browser, for example over SSH, set
`ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "UseDeviceCode": true }` in `maester-config.json`.

### Sign in as a service principal

In a pipeline, or anywhere nobody can sign in, connect Maester to Graph app-only with a certificate. The
assessment uses the same app and certificate, found by its thumbprint in the certificate store. A client secret, a
managed identity or workload identity federation is enough for Maester's own tests, but the assessment signs in
app-only only with a certificate.

```powershell
Import-Module ZeroTrustAssessment
Get-ZtGraphScope    # the Graph application permissions to give the app

Connect-MgGraph -ClientId <app id> -TenantId <tenant id> -CertificateThumbprint <thumbprint> -NoWelcome
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -NonInteractive
```

To leave out the assessment's Azure, Exchange Online, Security & Compliance and SharePoint tests, which need extra
roles for the app, set `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "Service": ["Graph"] }`.

### Read a report you already have

Run the assessment as its own step, then point Maester at the report it wrote:

```powershell
Connect-ZtAssessment
Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path ./zt -NoBrowser
```

```json
{ "GlobalSettings": { "ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath": "./zt" } }
```

Then, in a new PowerShell session, run `Connect-Maester` and `Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA`.

The assessment can take an hour or more on a large tenant. All its settings, a GitHub Actions workflow and how its
results map are on [maester.dev/docs/next/packs/zero-trust-assessment](https://maester.dev/docs/next/packs/zero-trust-assessment).

The Zero Trust Assessment is © Microsoft Corporation and published under the
[MIT licence](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment/blob/main/LICENSE). This pack does not include
its code: it runs the module you install, or reads the report it wrote.

    Returns one ZTA instance per result of the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Instance source of the ZTA family. Reads the assessment's ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json from the
    ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath setting when one is set (import), otherwise runs the assessment in a child
    PowerShell process (collect), then returns one instance per test result. Skips the whole family, with the
    reason, when neither is possible.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    $reportPath = [string](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath' -Default '')
    $collected = $null
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($reportPath)) {
        $collected = Invoke-MtZtaCollection
        $reportPath = $collected.ReportPath
    }

    try {
        $report = Read-MtZtaReport -Path $reportPath
        $context = Get-MgContext
        if ($context -and $context.TenantId -and $report.TenantId -and $report.TenantId -ne $context.TenantId) {
            Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "The Zero Trust Assessment report at $reportPath is for tenant $($report.TenantId), but Maester is connected to tenant $($context.TenantId)."
        }

        $maxAgeDays = [int](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays' -Default 7)
        # ConvertFrom-Json reads the ISO date as a DateTime already; text is parsed invariantly, never in the current culture.
        $executedAt = [datetime]::MinValue
        $hasDate = if ($report.ExecutedAt -is [datetime]) { $executedAt = $report.ExecutedAt; $true }
        elseif ($report.ExecutedAt -is [datetimeoffset]) { $executedAt = $report.ExecutedAt.UtcDateTime; $true }
        else {
            [datetime]::TryParse([string]$report.ExecutedAt, [cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture,
                [System.Globalization.DateTimeStyles]::AdjustToUniversal -bor [System.Globalization.DateTimeStyles]::AssumeUniversal, [ref]$executedAt)
        }
        if ($maxAgeDays -gt 0 -and $hasDate -and $executedAt.ToUniversalTime() -lt [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$maxAgeDays)) {
            Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "The Zero Trust Assessment report at $reportPath was written on $($executedAt.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')), more than $maxAgeDays days ago. Run Invoke-ZtAssessment again, or raise the ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays setting."
        }

        Add-MtZtaReportAttachment -ReportPath $reportPath
        ConvertTo-MtZtaInstance -Report $report
    } finally {
        # A collection into a temporary folder leaves nothing behind: the export holds raw tenant data.
        if ($collected -and $collected.Temporary -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $collected.OutputPath)) {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $collected.OutputPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        }
    }
}

function Add-MtZtaReportAttachment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Embeds the assessment's own HTML report in the Maester report, opened with one click.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The assessment writes ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html in the folder given to Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path, beside
    its zt-export folder. It is read before a temporary output folder is deleted. Nothing is attached when the
    report is not there (an imported report file copied on its own), when the ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport
    setting is false, or on a Maester version without Add-MtReportAttachment.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        # The report file, the assessment's output folder, or its zt-export folder.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $ReportPath
    )

    if (-not [bool](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport' -Default $true)) { return }
    if (-not (Get-Command -Name Add-MtReportAttachment -ErrorAction Ignore)) { return }

    $folder = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ReportPath -PathType Container) { $ReportPath } else { Split-Path -Path $ReportPath -Parent }
    if (-not $folder) { return }
    $html = @(
        (Join-Path $folder 'ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html'),
        (Join-Path (Split-Path -Path $folder -Parent) 'ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html')
    ) | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ -PathType Leaf) } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($html) {
        Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path $html
    } else {
        Write-Verbose "No ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html next to $ReportPath, so the assessment's own report is not embedded."
    }
}

function Read-MtZtaReport {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Reads ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json from a file, or from a folder the assessment wrote.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # The report file, the assessment's output folder, or its zt-export folder.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path
    )

    $file = $Path
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Container) {
        $file = @(
            (Join-Path $Path 'ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json'),
            (Join-Path -Path $Path -ChildPath 'zt-export' -AdditionalChildPath 'ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json')
        ) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ -PathType Leaf } | Select-Object -First 1
    }
    if (-not $file -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file -PathType Leaf)) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "No Zero Trust Assessment report was found at $Path. Point the ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath setting at ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json, or clear it to let Maester run the assessment."
    }

    $report = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file -Raw -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json -Depth 20
    if (-not $report.PSObject.Properties['Tests']) {
        throw "$file is not a Zero Trust Assessment report: it has no Tests list."
    }
    $report
}

function ConvertTo-MtZtaInstance {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Turns the Tests of a Zero Trust Assessment report into ZTA instances.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The instance suffix is the assessment's test ID. A test that writes several rows under one ID (the Defender
    for Cloud recommendations do) gets a suffix made from a hash of each row's title, so a row keeps its ID from
    one run to the next. Rows that share a title as well are numbered in report order. Planned tests, which the assessment lists but has not built, are left out.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # A report read by Read-MtZtaReport.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] $Report
    )

    $severity = @{ High = 'High'; Medium = 'Medium'; Low = 'Low' }
    $rows = @($Report.Tests | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.TestStatus -ne 'Planned' -and $_.TestSkipped -ne 'UnderConstruction' })
    $repeated = @($rows | Group-Object -Property { [string]$_.TestId } | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | ForEach-Object Name)
    $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create()
    try {
        foreach ($row in $rows) {
            $id = ([string]$row.TestId -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9._-]', '_') -replace '^[^A-Za-z0-9]+', ''
            if (-not $id) { continue }
            if ([string]$row.TestId -in $repeated) {
                $hash = $sha.ComputeHash([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes([string]$row.TestTitle))
                $id = '{0}.{1}' -f $id, ([System.Convert]::ToHexString($hash).Substring(0, 10).ToLowerInvariant())
            }
            $unique = $id
            for ($n = 2; -not $seen.Add($unique); $n++) { $unique = "$id.$n" }
            $id = $unique
            $tags = @('ZeroTrust') + @(@($row.TestPillar) | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { "ZeroTrust.$_" })
            $instance = [ordered]@{
                Id     = $id
                Title  = ([string]$row.TestTitle -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
                Tag    = $tags
                # Shown by the report, which groups the pack's results by pillar and category.
                Fields = [ordered]@{ Pillar = @($row.TestPillar | Where-Object { $_ }); Category = [string]$row.TestCategory }
                Data   = $row
            }
            if ($severity.ContainsKey([string]$row.TestRisk)) { $instance.Severity = $severity[[string]$row.TestRisk] }
            [pscustomobject]$instance
        }
    } finally {
        $sha.Dispose()
    }
}

function Invoke-MtZtaCollection {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Runs the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment in a child PowerShell process and returns where it wrote its report.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The assessment loads its own pinned versions of the Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online and Az modules and of
    MSAL, which cannot share a process with the versions Maester has already loaded. So it runs in its own
    pwsh process, signs in there with Connect-ZtAssessment, and Maester reads the report it writes.

    The child's output is read line by line and shown with Write-MtTestOutput: in the dashboard of an
    interactive run it scrolls in a box in the main column, elsewhere it is written to the host. The
    assessment runs with -ShowLog (the ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog setting, on by default), so the box shows
    the tests it runs, and its progress bars become one line at the bottom of the box that updates in place.

    The child also reports where the assessment is, read from the progress the module keeps for its own
    progress page and from the progress logs it writes: the stage, the exports or tests done of how many,
    the ones running, and each one that fails. It writes these as ##maester[progress] and ##maester[error]
    lines, which Write-MtTestOutput shows at the top of the box (see Write-MtTestProgress).

    The child signs in to the tenant Maester is connected to. When Maester is connected to Graph app-only with a
    certificate, the child uses the same app and certificate; otherwise it signs in interactively. The
    ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect setting passes any other Connect-ZtAssessment parameters.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    $module = Get-Module -Name ZeroTrustAssessment -ListAvailable | Sort-Object -Property Version -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $module) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'The ZeroTrustAssessment module is not installed. Run Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser, or set ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath to a report from an earlier run.'
    }

    $outputPath = [string](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath' -Default '')
    $temporary = [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($outputPath)
    if ($temporary) {
        $outputPath = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("maester-zta-{0}" -f [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('n'))
    } elseif ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $outputPath) -and @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $outputPath -Force).Count -gt 0) {
        # Invoke-ZtAssessment deletes a non-empty output folder, so each run gets its own folder under it.
        $outputPath = Join-Path $outputPath (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss')
    }
    $null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $outputPath -Force

    $connect = [ordered]@{}
    $context = Get-MgContext
    $connectSetting = Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect' -Default $null
    if ($context) {
        if ($context.TenantId) { $connect.TenantId = $context.TenantId }
        if ([string]$context.AuthType -eq 'AppOnly') {
            # Connected with a certificate object, the context names it in Certificate rather than CertificateThumbprint.
            $thumbprint = [string]$context.CertificateThumbprint
            if (-not $thumbprint -and $context.PSObject.Properties['Certificate'] -and $context.Certificate) { $thumbprint = [string]$context.Certificate.Thumbprint }
            if ($thumbprint) {
                $connect.ClientId = $context.ClientId
                $connect.Certificate = $thumbprint
            } elseif (-not $connectSetting) {
                # Connect-ZtAssessment signs in app-only with a certificate only; without one the child would wait for a person to sign in.
                Remove-Item -LiteralPath $outputPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
                Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'Maester is connected app-only without a certificate (a client secret, a managed identity or workload identity federation), and the Zero Trust Assessment signs in app-only only with a certificate. Connect Maester with a certificate in the certificate store, set ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect, or run Invoke-ZtAssessment as its own step and set ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath.'
                return
            }
        }
    }
    if ($connectSetting) {
        foreach ($property in $connectSetting.PSObject.Properties) { $connect[$property.Name] = $property.Value }
    }

    $assessment = [ordered]@{
        Path             = $outputPath
        Pillar           = [string](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.Pillar' -Default 'All')
        NoBrowser        = $true
        DisableTelemetry = [bool](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.DisableTelemetry' -Default $true)
        ShowLog          = [bool](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog' -Default $true)
    }
    $days = Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.Days' -Default $null
    if ($days) { $assessment.Days = [int]$days }
    $tests = @(Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.Tests' -Default @()) | Where-Object { $_ }
    if ($tests.Count -gt 0) { $assessment.Tests = [string[]]$tests }

    # The assessment reads emergency access accounts from its own configuration file, in the same shape as
    # Maester's GlobalSettings.EmergencyAccessAccounts.
    $emergencyAccounts = @(@(Get-MtSetting -Name 'EmergencyAccessAccounts' -Default @()) | Where-Object { $_ })
    $configurationFile = $null
    if ($emergencyAccounts.Count -gt 0) {
        $configurationFile = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("maester-zta-config-{0}.json" -f [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('n'))
        # @() keeps one account a JSON array.
        @{ GlobalSettings = @{ EmergencyAccessAccounts = @($emergencyAccounts) } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $configurationFile -Encoding utf8
        $assessment.ConfigurationFile = $configurationFile
    }

    $request = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("maester-zta-request-{0}.json" -f [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('n'))
    # The titles and pillars of the assessment's tests, from the pack's catalog, for the tests the progress lists
    # by ID, and how many tests each pillar has, for the dashboard's list of pillars. A test in two pillars counts
    # in its first.
    $titles = @{}
    $pillars = @{}
    $pillarTotals = [ordered]@{}
    $catalogPath = Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath 'catalog.json'
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $catalogPath) {
        foreach ($entry in @((Get-Content -LiteralPath $catalogPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).Tests)) {
            $titles[[string]$entry.TestId] = [string]$entry.Title
            $pillar = @($entry.Pillar | Where-Object { $_ }) | Select-Object -First 1
            if (-not $pillar -or ($assessment.Pillar -and $assessment.Pillar -ne 'All' -and $pillar -ne $assessment.Pillar)) { continue }
            $pillars[[string]$entry.TestId] = [string]$pillar
            $pillarTotals[[string]$pillar] = 1 + [int]$pillarTotals[[string]$pillar]
        }
    }
    $pillarList = @(foreach ($name in $pillarTotals.Keys) { [ordered]@{ Name = $name; Total = $pillarTotals[$name] } })
    [ordered]@{ ModulePath = $module.Path; Connect = $connect; Assessment = $assessment; Titles = $titles; Pillars = $pillars; PillarTotals = $pillarList } |
        ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $request -Encoding utf8

    # The child reads its parameters from the request file, so nothing from the config is put on a command line.
    # Its output is read by Maester as lines of plain text. Its progress bars cannot be drawn there, so each
    # change of one is written as a line that starts with a marker (the module's own Write-Progress calls find
    # this function before the cmdlet), which Maester shows as one line that updates in place.
    $progressMarker = "[maester-progress-$([guid]::NewGuid().ToString('n').Substring(0, 8))] "
    $script = @'
param([string] $RequestPath, [string] $ProgressMarker)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
$PSStyle.OutputRendering = 'PlainText'
function global:Write-Progress {
    # Not an advanced function: a parameter it does not declare goes to $args instead of failing the call.
    param([string] $Activity, [string] $Status, [int] $Id, [int] $PercentComplete = -1, [string] $CurrentOperation, [switch] $Completed)
    if ($Completed) {
        # An empty line of progress takes the line away.
        if ($global:__MtZtaProgress) { [Console]::Out.WriteLine($ProgressMarker) }
        $global:__MtZtaProgress = $null
        return
    }
    $text = @($Activity, $Status, $CurrentOperation) | Where-Object { $_ }
    $text = $text -join ': '
    if ($PercentComplete -ge 0) { $text += " ($PercentComplete%)" }
    if ($text -and $text -ne $global:__MtZtaProgress) {
        $global:__MtZtaProgress = $text
        [Console]::Out.WriteLine($ProgressMarker + $text)
    }
}
$request = Get-Content -LiteralPath $RequestPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
Import-Module -Name $request.ModulePath

137:    <#
138:    .SYNOPSIS
139:    Returns one ZTA instance per result of the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment.
140:
141:    .DESCRIPTION
142:    Instance source of the ZTA family. Reads the assessment's ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json from the
143:    ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath setting when one is set (import), otherwise runs the assessment in a child
144:    PowerShell process (collect), then returns one instance per test result. Skips the whole family, with the
145:    reason, when neither is possible.
146:    #>
147:    [CmdletBinding()]
148:    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
149:    param()
150:
151:    $reportPath = [string](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath' -Default '')
152:    $collected = $null
153:    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($reportPath)) {
154:        $collected = Invoke-MtZtaCollection
155:        $reportPath = $collected.ReportPath
156:    }

158:    try {

162:            Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "The Zero Trust Assessment report at $reportPath is for tenant $($report.TenantId), but Maester is connected to tenant $($context.TenantI
163:        }
164:
165:        $maxAgeDays = [int](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays' -Default 7)
166:        # ConvertFrom-Json reads the ISO date as a DateTime already; text is parsed invariantly, never in the current culture.
167:        $executedAt = [datetime]::MinValue
168:        $hasDate = if ($report.ExecutedAt -is [datetime]) { $executedAt = $report.ExecutedAt; $true }
169:        elseif ($report.ExecutedAt -is [datetimeoffset]) { $executedAt = $report.ExecutedAt.UtcDateTime; $true }
170:        else {
171:            [datetime]::TryParse([string]$report.ExecutedAt, [cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture,
172:                [System.Globalization.DateTimeStyles]::AdjustToUniversal -bor [System.Globalization.DateTimeStyles]::AssumeUniversal, [ref]$executedAt)
173:        }
174:        if ($maxAgeDays -gt 0 -and $hasDate -and $executedAt.ToUniversalTime() -lt [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$maxAgeDays)) {
175:            Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "The Zero Trust Assessment report at $reportPath was written on $($executedAt.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')), more than $maxAgeDays days ago. Ru

251:function ConvertTo-MtZtaInstance {
252:    <#
253:    .SYNOPSIS
254:    Turns the Tests of a Zero Trust Assessment report into ZTA instances.
255:
256:    .DESCRIPTION
257:    The instance suffix is the assessment's test ID. A test that writes several rows under one ID (the Defender
258:    for Cloud recommendations do) gets a suffix made from a hash of each row's title, so a row keeps its ID from
259:    one run to the next. Rows that share a title as well are numbered in report order. Planned tests, which the assessment lists but has not built, are left out.
260:    #>
261:    [CmdletBinding()]
262:    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
263:    param(
264:        # A report read by Read-MtZtaReport.
265:        [Parameter(Mandatory)] $Report
266:    )
267:
268:    $severity = @{ High = 'High'; Medium = 'Medium'; Low = 'Low' }
269:    $rows = @($Report.Tests | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.TestStatus -ne 'Planned' -and $_.TestSkipped -ne 'UnderConstruction' })
270:    $repeated = @($rows | Group-Object -Property { [string]$_.TestId } | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | ForEach-Object Name)
271:    $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
272:    $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create()
273:    try {
274:        foreach ($row in $rows) {
275:            $id = ([string]$row.TestId -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9._-]', '_') -replace '^[^A-Za-z0-9]+', ''
276:            if (-not $id) { continue }
277:            if ([string]$row.TestId -in $repeated) {
278:                $hash = $sha.ComputeHash([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes([string]$row.TestTitle))
279:                $id = '{0}.{1}' -f $id, ([System.Convert]::ToHexString($hash).Substring(0, 10).ToLowerInvariant())
280:            }
281:            $unique = $id
282:            for ($n = 2; -not $seen.Add($unique); $n++) { $unique = "$id.$n" }
283:            $id = $unique
284:            $tags = @('ZeroTrust') + @(@($row.TestPillar) | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { "ZeroTrust.$_" })
285:            $instance = [ordered]@{
286:                Id     = $id
287:                Title  = ([string]$row.TestTitle -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
288:                Tag    = $tags
289:                # Shown by the report, which groups the pack's results by pillar and category.
290:                Fields = [ordered]@{ Pillar = @($row.TestPillar | Where-Object { $_ }); Category = [string]$row.TestCategory }
291:                Data   = $row
292:            }
293:            if ($severity.ContainsKey([string]$row.TestRisk)) { $instance.Severity = $severity[[string]$row.TestRisk] }
294:            [pscustomobject]$instance
295:        }
296:    } finally {
297:        $sha.Dispose()
298:    }
299:}

﻿function Get-MtAffectedObjectTypeDefinition {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the curated object type catalog used to filter the affected objects.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Single source of truth for which object types count as an affected object.

    KnownTypes lists the systems whose Type values are a curated, enumerable set. A record of
    such a system whose Type is not listed is dropped by Get-MtAffectedObject and reported in a
    warning, so a new type is noticed and added here instead of silently reaching the report.

    Systems that are not listed in KnownTypes (MicrosoftGraph, ...) are pass-through: their Type
    is the Graph resource path, which is unbounded and cannot be enumerated.

    ExcludedTypes lists types that are recognised but are deliberately not inventoried — report
    findings and alerts describe a condition, not an addressable object. They are dropped
    without a warning.

    .EXAMPLE
    (Get-MtAffectedObjectTypeDefinition).KnownTypes.EntraID

    Lists the Entra ID object types that are listed as affected objects.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([hashtable])]
    param()

    return @{
        KnownTypes    = @{
            EntraID        = @(
                'AccessPackage'
                'AccessPackageCatalog'
                'AppRegistration'
                'AuthenticationMethod'
                'AuthorizationPolicy'
                'ConditionalAccessPolicy'
                'ConsentPolicy'
                'Device'
                'DirectoryRole'
                'Domains'
                'Group'
                'ServicePrincipal'
                'User'
            )
            DefenderXDR    = @(
                'Device'
            )
            ExchangeOnline = @(
                'SharingPolicy'
                'TransportRule'
            )
            GitHub         = @(
                'GitHubOrganization'
                'GitHubRepository'
                'GitHubResource'
            )
        }
        ExcludedTypes = @{
            # Entra recommendations and PIM alerts are findings about the tenant, not objects in it.
            EntraID = @(
                'EntraRecommendation'
                'PimAlert'
            )
        }
    }
}

input.recap: Plan ready, nothing changed yet. Replaying the current detection over the 24 Oct ZTA run already finds 303 objects across 42 ZT results. The gaps are agent identities, Intune policies, Azure resources, SAML apps with no object ID, and tables with no links.

content.text:
Here's the plan. One finding up front changes how much is needed.

## What the data shows

**Most ZT objects already reach the blade.** None of the past ZTA runs (23–24 Oct, 327 ZTA rows each) have an inventory, because they ran without affected objects. I replayed today's `Get-MtAffectedObject` over the ZTA rows of `test-results/TestResults-2026-10-24-092527.json`. The markdown parser already finds **303 objects across 42 ZT results**: 144 service principals, 67 app registrations, 60 users and 32 CA policies, nearly all with display names. ZT writes the same Entra deep links Maester's own tests write, so this already works with no new code. It still needs checking in a live run.

**What it misses** (from the 24 Oct run and the June raw sample in `maester-cloud/scripts/local-samples/zt`):

| Gap | Volume | Why it's missed |
|---|---|---|
| Agent identities and blueprints (`AgentIdentity.MenuView`, `AgentBlueprintDetails.MenuView`) | ~40 links, 3 results | No pattern or type for them |
| SAML apps linked as `objectId//appId/{guid}` | 14 links | The object ID is empty, so the service principal pattern fails |
| Intune policies (`PolicySummaryBlade/policyId/{guid}`) | 9 links | There's no Intune system yet |
| Azure subscriptions, VMs, VNets and Defender for Cloud recommendations per resource | ~97 links in the June sample | There's no Azure system yet |
| Tables that name objects with no link (e.g. ZTA.21775 app secrets, ZTA.22124 recommendations) | 10 results | Nothing to parse |
| Portal pages with no object (Intune config pages, auth methods) | many | These are pages, not objects. Leave them out. |

## Plan

**1. Core: object types a native port will need anyway (these stay).**
Add the types themselves, their link templates and their markdown patterns:
- **EntraID:** `AgentIdentity` and `AgentIdentityBlueprint`.
- **Intune** (new system): `ConfigurationPolicy`.
- **Azure** (new system): `Subscription` and `Resource`, both keyed by ARM ID.

The changes go in `Get-MtAffectedObjectTypeDefinition`, `Get-MtPortalLinkTemplate`, `Get-MtAffectedObjectFromMarkdown` and the README. The rule: anything a native Maester test would also emit belongs in core, because a ported test will use these types through `-GraphObjects`.

**2. Pack: one removable ZT step.**
Add one function, `ConvertTo-MtZtaRelatedObject`, in `packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests/Test.ZTA.ps1`. `Get-MtZtaInstance` calls it right after `Read-MtZtaReport`, which is after the assessment has run but before its temporary `zt-export` folder is deleted. For each row it:
- resolves the SAML `appId` links to the service principal's object ID, using the export's `ServicePrincipal` data;
- puts the records on the instance (`Instance.RelatedObjects`).

`Test-MtZeroTrustAssessment` then hands them to the engine. That needs one new, generic switch: `Add-MtTestResultDetail -AffectedObject`. It takes ready-made `{System, Type, Id, DisplayName}` records and runs them through `ConvertTo-MtAffectedObjectRecord`. Note that this makes it public API. Custom tests and the SCuBA packs could use it too.

**To remove it later:** delete the function, its single call and the `-AffectedObject` line in the test, or delete the pack. The core types and the switch stay, and native tests use them.

**Considered and rejected:** a post-run hook declared in `maester-pack.json` that `ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult` would call. It would add a manifest contract that has to be retired later. It would also run after the export is gone, and it gains nothing per result, since each row already knows its own objects.

**3. Optional (phase 2): link-less tables.** Match names in the tables against the export's `Application`, `ServicePrincipal` and `User` data to get IDs. This only works when Maester ran the assessment itself, or when the imported folder includes `zt-export`. I'd leave it out unless you want it.

**4. Checks**
- Unit tests for the new patterns in `Get-MtAffectedObject.Tests.ps1`.
- A small redacted fixture in `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1`.
- Re-run the offline replay on the 24 Oct run and the June sample to confirm the new types show up. The June sample is a raw ZT report, so it needs converting to Maester rows first.
- One live `Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA` run to see the blade itself.

**Defaults I'd use unless you say otherwise:**
- Objects from **passed** ZT results stay in, as they do for native tests. The page already filters by result.
- Defender incidents and Entra recommendations stay excluded as findings, as they are today.

Merill asked (2026-11-05) how undrgrnd-labs/hunch could make the Maester report more insightful, and for a full plan. Published as a private artifact: https://claude.ai/artifact/Xtiz4DyW2n7MEwZujQbNAG (source in that session's scratchpad only; nothing in the repo, per the rule that research stays out of Maester).

Core recommendations: an insights step after the tests (`Insight.<ID>.ps1`, packs can ship them, typed `Insights` records with evidence, prefix `MI.`). Tier A uses only result data: attack scenarios + choke points, most exposed identities, fix-once groups, trends, template summary. Tier B adds bounded reads: measured user impact from sign-in logs and report-only CA results, config snapshot + audit-log change attribution, licence value. Tier C is opt-in question models: critical assets by meaning, suspicious objects, CA intent check, optional AI summary with citation check. Plus a reader profile (infer first, then 5 questions) that re-ranks but never hides findings.

input.recap: Read the ZT export code on main and queried your 23 Oct db. It holds 17 entity tables (no general Groups table), and they support per-object facts plus a set of cross-object insights. Nothing changed in the repo.
input.ask: Which scope for the first build?

content.text:
Yes, the export has enough to enrich the report well beyond object IDs. I queried your 23 Oct `zt-export` (DuckDB opened read-only from a copy) and read the ZT export code on `microsoft/zerotrustassessment` main.

## What the export holds

ZT main exports 17 entities. Your 23 Oct run matches that list:

- **Apps:** `Application` (174), `ServicePrincipal` (865, with app role assignments and delegated grants expanded), `ServicePrincipalSignIn` (591)
- **Agents:** `AgentIdentity`, `AgentIdentityBlueprint`, `AgentIdentityBlueprintPrincipal`
- **Users:** `User` (with `signInActivity` on P1+), `UserRegistrationDetails`
- **Roles:** role definitions, permanent and eligible assignments, PIM policies, plus a `vwRole` view that merges them with privileged-group members
- **Devices and Intune:** `Device`, `ConfigurationPolicy` (with assignments)
- **Sign-ins:** `SignIn`, a capped sample (147 rows over 30 days here)

**There is no general Groups table.** Groups appear only as members of privileged (PIM) groups.

**Maester doesn't need DuckDB.** The `db` is built from plain Graph JSON pages (`zt-export/<Entity>/<Entity>-N.json`, `{ "value": [...] }`), so Maester can read those directly. That avoids loading ZT's DuckDB.NET into Maester's process. 51 ZT tests query the db, mostly `ServicePrincipal`, `ConfigurationPolicy`, `Application` and `vwRole`.

## What we can pull, with your tenant's numbers

**1. Facts on each object in the Affected objects blade** (the most useful, and the easiest to remove later):

| Object | Facts | Your tenant |
|---|---|---|
| App / service principal | First- or third-party, publisher, last sign-in, Graph app permissions (names resolved from Graph's own `appRoles`), tenant-wide delegated consent and its scopes, secret and certificate expiry, owner count | 488 of 591 apps have no sign-in in 90 days; 59 secrets already expired; 142 of 174 apps have no owner |
| User | Roles (permanent or eligible), MFA registered, methods, passwordless capable, last sign-in, guest or synced | 47 members, 22 of them stale |
| Device | Compliant, managed, trust type, last sign-in | 18 of 26 stale |
| Agent identity / blueprint | Sponsor, owners, has a secret, which blueprint | All 16 blueprints have no owner; 12 have secrets |
| Intune policy | Assigned or not, platform, setting count | 20 policies |

**2. Cross-object insights.** These are the joins no single test makes. They fit the Tier B "insights step" in the report-intelligence plan, and they fill the gap that plan found (no shared app or service principal data, and sign-in logs read by only one check):

- **Admins without MFA:** 6 privileged users, 3 of them Global Admins.
- **Risky apps:** apps that combine powerful permissions with an expired secret, no owner, or no recent sign-in.
- **Tenant-wide delegated consent with write scopes:** for example, Lokka has `Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess` for all users.
- **Permanent privileged assignments:** 9 users and 4 service principals.
- **Single-factor sign-ins:** 144 of the 147 sampled interactive sign-ins, with no CA policy applied. This must be labelled as ZT's sample, not the whole log.

**3. Filling the 10 ZT result tables that list objects with no link** (e.g. ZTA.21775 app secrets), by matching the names against the export.

## Constraints

- **When the data is there:** after a collection run, the export sits in a temp folder that `Get-MtZtaInstance` deletes, so the read has to happen before that `finally`. In import mode (`ReportPath`), it works only if the `zt-export` folder sits next to the report.
- **Which snapshot:** the data is ZT's snapshot, not Maester's session cache. I'd label every fact "from the Zero Trust Assessment, <ExecutedAt>". It is a separate source, not a cache bypass, but flag it if you see it differently.
- **Privacy:** these facts add more user detail to the report. They must go through the `-RedactUserIdentity` map, and the html copy should stay slim.
- **Overlap with Maester's own checks:** several facts (app credentials, admins without MFA) are things Maester checks too. Show them as facts and insights, not as new pass/fail rows, or the report gives two answers.

## Where the code goes

This extends the plan from my last message:

- **Pack (removable):** `Read-MtZtaExport` plus `ConvertTo-MtZtaObjectFact` in `Test.ZTA.ps1`, emitting through the `-AffectedObject` switch.
- **Core (stays):** a generic `Facts` bag on affected-object records, and rendering for it on the page. Native tests can fill it later.
- **Insights:** wait for the insights step, or start as a pack-side summary if you want them sooner.

69	  "identityProtection/settings/notifications": "Risk notification settings",
70	}

72	const guidSegment = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-(?:[0-9a-f]{4}-){3}[0-9a-f]{12}$/i
73	
74	// "accessPackageCatalogs" -> "Access package catalogs"
75	function sentenceCase(value: string) {
76	  const spaced = value.replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, "$1 $2")
77	  const words = spaced.split(" ").map((word, index) =>
78	    index === 0 ? word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1) : /^[A-Z][a-z]/.test(word) ? word.toLowerCase() : word
79	  )
80	  return words.join(" ").replace(/\b(Vpp|Ndes|Pim)\b/gi, (acronym) => acronym.toUpperCase())
81	}

83	export function getAffectedObjectTypeInfo(system: string, type: string): AffectedObjectTypeInfo {
84	  const known = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(knownTypes, type) ? knownTypes[type] : undefined
85	  if (known) {
86	    return { name: known[0], icon: known[1], area: systemNames[system] ?? system }
87	  }
88	
89	  const area = graphAreas.find(([prefix]) => type === prefix || type.startsWith(`${prefix}/`))
90	  const leaf = type.split("/").filter((segment) => !guidSegment.test(segment)).pop() ?? type
91	  const alert = leaf.match(/_([A-Za-z]+)Alert$/)
92	  const name = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(graphNames, type)
93	    ? graphNames[type]
94	    : alert
95	      ? `${sentenceCase(alert[1])} alert`
96	      : sentenceCase(leaf)
97	
98	  return {
99	    name,
100	    icon: area ? area[2] : "tenant",
101	    area: area ? area[1] : systemNames[system] ?? system,
102	  }
103	}

function Add-MtReportAttachment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Embeds an HTML report from another tool in the Maester HTML report, opened with one click.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Call this from a test, an instance source or a pack when the tool it runs writes its own single-file
    HTML report (for example the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment). The file is read at once, so the tool's
    output folder can be deleted afterwards.

    The HTML report shows a button for each attachment on the overview page, and on the result of the test
    that added it. The button shows the attached report inside the Maester report, beside its navigation, with an option to open it in a new browser tab. The report is stored compressed
    (gzip, then Base64), so a 10 MB report adds about 2 MB to the Maester report.

    Attachments are kept only in the HTML report and the results that Invoke-Maester -PassThru returns. The
    JSON results file lists each attachment's name and size without its content. The HTML report leaves
    attachments out when -RedactUserIdentity is used, because Maester cannot redact another tool's report.

    The attached page runs in a sandboxed frame, with its scripts in an origin of their own, so it cannot read or
    change the Maester report or its data. Adding a second attachment with the same name from the same test
    replaces the first.

    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path ./zt/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html

    Embeds the Zero Trust Assessment report in the Maester report of this run.

    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Tenant inventory' -Content $html

    Embeds an HTML page built in memory.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Add-MtReportAttachment
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName = 'Path')]
    [OutputType([void])]
    param(
        # The label of the button that opens the attachment, for example 'Zero Trust Assessment'.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Name,

        # Path of a single-file HTML report to embed.
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ParameterSetName = 'Path')]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Path,

        # The HTML to embed, when it is not in a file.
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ParameterSetName = 'Content')]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Content
    )

    if ($PSCmdlet.ParameterSetName -eq 'Path') {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Leaf)) {
            Write-Warning "Add-MtReportAttachment: $Path was not found, so '$Name' is not attached to the report."
            return
        }
        $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path).ProviderPath)
        $fileName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path)
    } else {
        $bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($Content)
        $fileName = $null
    }

    $buffer = [System.IO.MemoryStream]::new()
    try {
        $gzip = [System.IO.Compression.GZipStream]::new($buffer, [System.IO.Compression.CompressionLevel]::SmallestSize, $true)
        try { $gzip.Write($bytes, 0, $bytes.Length) } finally { $gzip.Dispose() }
        $compressed = [System.Convert]::ToBase64String($buffer.ToArray())
    } finally {
        $buffer.Dispose()
    }

    # The test that added it, so the report can show the button on that test's result too.
    $testId = [Maester.Engine.MtSession]::GetCurrentTest()

    if (-not $__MtSession.ReportAttachments) { $__MtSession.ReportAttachments = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new() }
    $existing = @($__MtSession.ReportAttachments | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $Name -and $_.TestId -eq $testId })

function Add-MtAffectedObjectFact {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Adds facts about an object, such as its last sign-in or its expired secrets, to the Affected objects page.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Call this from a test, an instance source or a pack that knows more about an object than the checks that name
    it: when the object was last used, which permissions it holds, whether its credentials have expired. The facts
    are shown with the object on the Affected objects page of the HTML report and kept in the AffectedObjects of the
    results, the JSON output and the objects files.

    Facts only describe an object that the run already lists. They are merged into the record with the same System,
    Type and Id when the results are built, so adding facts about an object that no check names adds nothing to the
    report. Facts are collected only while Invoke-Maester collects affected objects; otherwise the call does nothing.

    Each fact has a Name, a Value and a Tone: Risk for something to fix, Warning for something to review, Good for a
    sign that the object is in order, and Info (the default) for anything else. Adding a fact with the same Name from
    the same Source again replaces the earlier one.

    The value is shown as text. Name counts rather than other people where you can: the page shows facts to everyone
    who reads the report, and -RedactUserIdentity replaces only the names of users the run knows.

    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Type ServicePrincipal -Id $sp.id -Source 'Contoso inventory' -Fact @(
        @{ Name = 'Last sign-in'; Value = '2026-06-15 (143 days ago)'; Tone = 'Risk' }
        @{ Name = 'Publisher'; Value = 'Third party (Contoso Ltd)' }
    )

    Adds two facts to an enterprise application.

    .EXAMPLE
    $records | Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Source 'Zero Trust Assessment' -AsOf $report.ExecutedAt

    Adds facts to many objects at once. Each record has Type, Id and Fact properties, and optionally System.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Add-MtAffectedObjectFact
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([void])]
    param(
        # The object type, as the Affected objects page records it: User, Group, ServicePrincipal, AppRegistration
        # (keyed by its appId), Device, ConditionalAccessPolicy, AgentIdentity, AgentIdentityBlueprint, ConfigurationPolicy...
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Type,

        # The object's id, the same id the record uses (for an app registration, its appId).
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Id,

        # The facts: hashtables or objects with Name, Value and an optional Tone (Risk, Warning, Good or Info).
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [AllowEmptyCollection()]
        [object[]] $Fact,

        # Where the object lives: EntraID (the default), Intune, ExchangeOnline, GitHub...
        [Parameter(ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $System = 'EntraID',

        # What the facts come from, shown with them, for example 'Zero Trust Assessment'.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Source,

        # When the data behind the facts was read, when that is not now (a report written earlier).
        [Parameter()]
        [Nullable[datetime]] $AsOf
    )

    begin {
        $collecting = [bool]$__MtSession.IncludeAffectedObjects
        if (-not $collecting) {
            Write-Verbose 'Add-MtAffectedObjectFact: this run does not collect affected objects, so the facts are not kept.'
            return
        }
        if ($null -eq $__MtSession.AffectedObjectFacts) {
            $__MtSession.AffectedObjectFacts = [System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary[string, System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        }
        $asOfText = if ($null -ne $AsOf) { $AsOf.Value.ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ', [cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture) } else { $null }
        $tones = @('Risk', 'Warning', 'Good', 'Info')
    }

    process {
        if (-not $collecting) { return }

        $key = '{0}|{1}|{2}' -f $System, $Type, $Id
        $list = $null
        if (-not $__MtSession.AffectedObjectFacts.TryGetValue($key, [ref]$list)) {
            $list = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
            $__MtSession.AffectedObjectFacts[$key] = $list
        }

        foreach ($item in @($Fact)) {
            if ($null -eq $item) { continue }
            $name = [string](Get-ObjectProperty $item 'Name')
            $value = Get-ObjectProperty $item 'Value'
            if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($name) -or $null -eq $value -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$value)) { continue }
            $tone = [string](Get-ObjectProperty $item 'Tone')
            $tone = if ($tone) { $tones | Where-Object { $_ -eq $tone } | Select-Object -First 1 } else { 'Info' }
            if (-not $tone) {
                Write-Warning "Add-MtAffectedObjectFact: '$name' has the tone '$(Get-ObjectProperty $item 'Tone')', which is not Risk, Warning, Good or Info, so it is shown as Info."
                $tone = 'Info'
            }
            $text = ([string]$value).Trim()
            if ($text.Length -gt 300) { $text = $text.Substring(0, 299) + '…' }

            $index = $list.FindIndex({ param($existing) $existing.Name -eq $name -and $existing.Source -eq $Source })
            $record = [PSCustomObject]@{
                Name   = $name
                Value  = $text
                Tone   = $tone
                Source = $Source
                AsOf   = $asOfText
            }
            if ($index -ge 0) { $list[$index] = $record } else { $list.Add($record) }
        }
    }
}

function Get-RoleSelectSql {
		[CmdletBinding()]
		param (
			[Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
			[string]
			$TableName,

			[Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
			[string]
			$PrivilegeType,

			[switch]
			$AddUnion
		)
		$sql = @"

    select
        rd.isPrivileged,
        cast(r."roleDefinitionId" as varchar)           as roleDefinitionId,
        cast(r.principal.displayName as varchar)        as principalDisplayName,
        rd.displayName                                  as roleDisplayName,
        cast(r.principal.userPrincipalName as varchar)  as userPrincipalName,
        cast(r.principal.uniqueName as varchar)          as uniqueName,
        cast(r.principal."@odata.type" as varchar)      as "@odata.type",
        cast(r.principalId as varchar)                  as principalId,
        '$PrivilegeType'                                as privilegeType
    from main."$TableName" r
        left join main."RoleDefinition" rd on r."roleDefinitionId" = rd.id

	union all

    select
        rd2.isPrivileged,
        cast(r2."roleDefinitionId" as varchar)           as roleDefinitionId,
        cast(r2.displayName as varchar)        as principalDisplayName,
        rd2.displayName                                  as roleDisplayName,
        cast(r2.userPrincipalName as varchar)  as userPrincipalName,
        null                                   as uniqueName, -- *Group tables store members as flat rows with no principal struct, so uniqueName does not exist; null keeps this column aligned in the UNION ALL
        cast(r2."@odata.type" as varchar)      as "@odata.type",
        cast(r2.Id as varchar)                  as principalId,
        '$PrivilegeType'                        as privilegeType
    from main."$($TableName)Group" r2
        left join main."RoleDefinition" rd2 on r2."roleDefinitionId" = rd2.id

"@

		if ($AddUnion) {
			$sql += 'union all'
		}

		return $sql
	}

If the assessment runs somewhere else, or you'd rather keep the certificate out of the Maester step, run
`Connect-ZtAssessment -ClientId <app> -TenantId <tenant> -Certificate <thumbprint>` and
`Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path ./zt -NoBrowser` as their own step, then let Maester read the report with
`ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` (see [Read a report you already have](#read-a-report-you-already-have-recommended-in-ci)).
Maester's step can then connect any way it likes, including OIDC, as long as it is the same tenant.

## The assessment's own report

The Maester report embeds the HTML report the assessment wrote, with its pillar dashboards and charts. Open it
with the **Zero Trust Assessment** button on the report's overview, under **Reports** in the left menu, or on any
ZTA result. It opens inside the Maester report, with an option to open it in a new browser tab, and works
offline, so the Maester report stays a single file to share.

The embedded report is compressed: a 10 MB assessment report adds about 2 MB to the Maester report. It is left
out when `ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport` is `false`, when you read a report file that has no
`ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html` beside it or one folder up, and when `Invoke-Maester -RedactUserIdentity` is
used, because Maester cannot redact the assessment's report.

## Settings

All settings go in `GlobalSettings` of `maester-config.json`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` | empty | Read this report instead of running the assessment. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays` | `7` | Refuse a report older than this. `0` turns the check off. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport` | `true` | Embed the assessment's own HTML report in the Maester report. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath` | temporary | Where the assessment writes its report and export. Kept when set. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Pillar` | `All` | Run one pillar only: `Identity`, `Devices`, `Network`, `Data`, `Infrastructure`, `SecOps` or `AI`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Tests` | all | Run only these assessment test IDs, for example `["21770", "21771"]`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Days` | `30` | Days of sign-in logs the assessment reads (1 to 30). |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog` | `true` | Run the assessment with `-ShowLog`, which lists the tests it runs in its live output. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.DisableTelemetry` | `true` | The assessment sends the tenant ID to Microsoft unless this is `true`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` | none | Further `Connect-ZtAssessment` parameters, for example `{ "Service": ["Graph", "Azure"], "UseDeviceCode": true }`. |
